vuln_id: ARVO arvo:64622 / Pigweed pw_stream invalid downcast

project.name: Pigweed
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the local vulnerable checkout at `gt_results/arvo_64622/_work/src/pigweed`, which is clean at commit `581056821fdab2f257bbdc8aec67619f60c9c448`. That staged tree differs from the metadata `vulnerable_commit`, but it still contains the unfixed `static_cast`-based stream adapter code shown in `patch.diff`, and its `stream.h` / `uart_transport*.cc` line map matches the saved UBSan trace.

bug_description.original: pw_stream uses static_cast() to cast types up to a generic Stream and then down to a smaller API subset (such as stream::Writer) using static_cast. This downcast can sometimes be to a completely different type, which technically relies on undefined behavior. This undefined behavior is detectable during fuzz testing and can cause issues such as UBSAN errors. The vulnerability lies in pw::stream::Stream relying on undefined behavior when casting between unrelated types using static_cast in stream adapters.
bug_description.original_source: CyberGym tasks.json / sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 3-byte UART blob `04 20 00`. In `DecodeHciUartData()`, byte `0x04` is read as `packet_indicator` and selects the `kUartEventPacketIndicator` branch; `EventPacket::Decode()` then reads the third PoC byte `0x00` as the packet's `parameter_total_length`, sees that the 2-byte event header is complete, and materializes an `EventPacket` with `event_code == 0x20` and empty parameters. `DecodeHciUartData()` therefore invokes the fuzz callback with that decoded packet. At the top of the callback, before the `switch (packet.type())` or any `stream.Write()`, `stream::Writer& stream = stream::NullStream::Instance();` asks the singleton `NullStream` to convert to `Writer&`. `NullStream` inherits `SeekableReaderWriter -> RelativeSeekableReaderWriter -> ReaderWriter`, so the inherited `ReaderWriter::operator Writer&()` forwards to `as_writer()`, whose vulnerable implementation does `static_cast<Writer&>(static_cast<Stream&>(*this))`. For a `NullStream` object there is no `Writer` base subobject, so this downcast is invalid and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer reports `downcast of pw::stream::NullStream to pw::stream::Writer` at `pw_stream/public/pw_stream/stream.h:486`. The fix rewrites `as_reader()` / `as_writer()` and the related adapter casts to `std::launder(reinterpret_cast<...>(this))`, removing the UB-triggering `static_cast` downcast path.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled UART bytes and materializes the packet-type dispatch key that selects the parser branch leading to the crashing callback.
source.value_from: The staged PoC `gt_results/arvo_64622/poc` is exactly `04 20 00` (sha256 `8a1d8c403c17e83bcd6c1f5305642094103049f8896b5a00a645e871576d5c23`). Byte 0 is `0x04`, which equals `kUartEventPacketIndicator` and routes the remaining bytes into `EventPacket::Decode()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first attacker-derived parser state on the crashing path is the UART packet-indicator byte. It decides which packet decoder runs and whether a callback is reached.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `ReaderWriter::as_writer()` assumes any `ReaderWriter`-derived object may be downcast from its `Stream` base to `Writer&` with `static_cast`, even when the dynamic object is `NullStream`, which inherits `SeekableReaderWriter` rather than `Writer` and has no `Writer` base subobject.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact adapter to `*std::launder(reinterpret_cast<Writer*>(this))`, confirming that the vulnerable obligation is the invalid `static_cast` downcast itself.

sink.description: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer crash site. The callback's request for a `Writer&` from `NullStream::Instance()` reaches this cast and UBSan reports the invalid downcast here.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace names `as_writer` at `pw_stream/public/pw_stream/stream.h:486:12` and records that the object at this address is `pw::stream::NullStream`, not `pw::stream::Writer`.

parser_admitted.description: After reading the first input byte as `0x04`, the UART parser admits the witness into the event-packet branch and calls `EventPacket::Decode()` on the remaining bytes `20 00`.

coarse_trace.summary: The 3-byte witness is parsed as one complete HCI UART event packet: byte `0x04` selects the event branch, the length byte is `0`, and `EventPacket::Decode()` returns an `EventPacket` with `event_code == 0x20` and empty parameters.

Because the event packet decoded successfully, `DecodeHciUartData()` invokes the callback. The callback immediately tries to bind `stream::NullStream::Instance()` to `stream::Writer&` before inspecting `packet.type()` or writing packet fields.

The inherited `ReaderWriter` adapter forwards the `NullStream` object into `as_writer()`, which performs `static_cast<Writer&>(static_cast<Stream&>(*this))`. Because `NullStream` has no `Writer` base subobject, UBSan reports the invalid downcast at `stream.h:486`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first attacker-controlled byte is materialized as the UART packet indicator. For the staged witness, `packet_indicator == std::byte{0x04}`.
Because `packet_indicator` is the event-packet discriminator, the switch enters the event branch and passes the remaining bytes `20 00` to `EventPacket::Decode()`.

After the UART indicator is popped, `EventPacket::Decode()` sees `data == 20 00`; its length read uses `data[1]`, so the third PoC byte, `0x00`, becomes `parameter_total_length`. Here `parameter_total_length == 0`.

The completeness guard uses the same 2-byte decode span plus the parsed length. After the UART byte is removed, `data.size_bytes() == 2`, and `kHeaderSizeBytes + parameter_total_length == 2`, so the guard is false and the packet is accepted as complete.

The same 2-byte span also supplies the returned packet fields: `data[0]` becomes `event_code == 0x20`, and `data.subspan(kHeaderSizeBytes, parameter_total_length)` is empty because the decoded length is zero.
With a decoded event packet present, `DecodeHciUartData()` invokes the callback. Reaching this call is the last parser-side control decision needed for the vulnerability.

When `packet_callback(packet)` enters the lambda body, line 32 executes before the `switch (packet.type())` or any `stream.Write()`. This statement asks the singleton `NullStream` to bind to a `Writer&`, which uses the inherited `ReaderWriter` conversion operator on a `NullStream` object.

Root cause and sink. `as_writer()` executes the downcast on the same `NullStream` object requested in step 7. Because `NullStream` derives from `SeekableReaderWriter` / `ReaderWriter` and not from `Writer`, the `Stream` subobject has no valid `Writer` child, so UBSan reports `downcast of pw::stream::NullStream to pw::stream::Writer` at this exact cast.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_64622 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduced `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior downcast of pw::stream::NullStream to pw::stream::Writer` at `pw_stream/public/pw_stream/stream.h:486:12`, with the project stack `as_writer -> pw::stream::ReaderWriter::operator pw::stream::Writer&() -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput::$_0::operator()`.

format.name: 3-byte HCI UART event packet
format.contract: Exactly the staged 3-byte blob `04 20 00` in `gt_results/arvo_64622/poc` (sha256 `8a1d8c403c17e83bcd6c1f5305642094103049f8896b5a00a645e871576d5c23`). Byte 0 `0x04` is `kUartEventPacketIndicator`, byte 1 `0x20` becomes the event code, and byte 2 `0x00` makes `parameter_total_length == 0`, so `EventPacket::Decode()` returns a complete packet and `DecodeHciUartData()` invokes the callback that immediately performs the invalid `NullStream` -> `Writer&` conversion before inspecting `packet.type()`.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 is limited to the single saved vulnerable UBSan reproduction plus the staged source, patch, PoC, and report artifacts; it did not rerun the target or collect any new dynamic evidence.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false and `trace_feedback.json` does not request it, so Stage 02 did not instrument the C++ adapter path; the `NullStream -> ReaderWriter::operator Writer&() -> as_writer()` chain is source-grounded from the saved stack and the staged class hierarchy only.
Neither Stage 01 nor Stage 02 executed the fixed image for this sample, so the `patch_resolves` assessment is source-grounded from `patch.diff` rather than from vulnerable/fixed differential rerun.
